JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset serves as a placeholder or reference point for the foundational data underlying analyst estimates and key performance indicators, without containing any actual financial or market data itself. Its primary function is to facilitate access to industry classifications and essential metadata required for quantitative research, while avoiding penalization for using common base modules in research workflows. Although it does not provide direct content, it enables seamless integration of industry and company classification information, which is crucial for constructing and interpreting analyst-driven signals and for ensuring consistency in backtesting and model development. By supporting the structural backbone for more detailed analyst and KPI datasets, it indirectly aids in the accurate prediction of price movements through proper sector and industry alignment.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Standardized Analyst Consensus Forecasts
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides standardized, cleaned, and event-aligned analyst consensus forecasts and actuals for global equities, enabling direct comparison across companies and time. It aggregates and harmonizes consensus data from multiple leading sources, including I/B/E/S, Capital IQ, and FactSet, and applies rigorous data cleaning to remove expired or irrelevant forecasts. The dataset supports flexible configuration for different forecast horizons (quarterly, annual, rolling) and includes both forecast and actual values, as well as surprise calculations. By offering time-series event data with consistent methodology, it allows users to track revisions, analyze forecast accuracy, and construct robust quantitative models. This makes it a valuable resource for predicting price movements, backtesting strategies, and understanding market expectations versus realized outcomes.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Global Analyst Earnings Forecasts
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global analyst earnings forecasts, consensus estimates, and actuals for over 60,000 companies, sourced from broker and sell-side analyst submissions. It includes detailed and summary-level data on key financial metrics such as earnings per share (EPS), revenue, cash flow, and segment-level results, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The dataset tracks both current and historical estimates, revisions, and company-issued guidance, with extensive metadata on contributors, accounting standards, and industry classifications. By aggregating and updating analyst expectations in near real-time, this dataset enables users to monitor market sentiment, identify earnings momentum, and anticipate potential surprises—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing quantitative investment strategies.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Global Analyst Factor Signals
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of analyst-derived quantitative factors and indicators for global equities, constructed using standardized methodologies. It leverages consensus estimates, actuals, and revision data from multiple sources to generate a wide range of predictive signals, such as estimate momentum, earnings surprise, and analyst recommendation trends. The dataset is designed to be comparable across regions and time, with rigorous data cleaning and normalization. By offering both raw and composite factors—similar to those used in established quantitative models—this resource enables users to systematically test and implement alpha strategies, enhance risk models, and improve the forecasting of price movements based on analyst behavior and expectations.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Multi Horizon Analyst Revision Signals
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides decomposed analyst revision signals across short, medium, and long time horizons, derived from a comprehensive analyst revision-based stock ranking model. By applying advanced signal processing techniques, it extracts horizon-specific components from a wide array of analyst-driven metrics, such as earnings estimate changes, recommendation shifts, and predicted surprises. The resulting fields enable researchers and investors to isolate and analyze the impact of analyst sentiment and estimate revisions over different time frames, enhancing the ability to identify timely alpha opportunities and anticipate price movements driven by changes in analyst outlook. This multi-horizon approach is particularly valuable for constructing and testing trading strategies that are sensitive to the timing and persistence of analyst-driven signals.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Behavioral Finance Signal Factors
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a suite of behavioral finance-based signals designed to capture investor extrapolation bias in equity markets. It includes six key factors: three that analyze the shape and curvature of price paths, and three that identify salient patterns such as streaks in returns, extreme daily movements, and visually prominent trends. By quantifying how investors may irrationally project recent performance into the future, these signals serve as contrarian indicators and can help forecast short-term reversals and momentum effects. The dataset is valuable for predictive modeling, risk assessment, and portfolio construction, offering insights into market inefficiencies driven by psychological biases and aiding in the identification of potential mispricings and alpha opportunities.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: user predictions from Minkabu
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset aggregates stock price predictions made by retail investors across major social media platforms in Japan, Europe, and China. It includes detailed records of buy/sell recommendations, target prices, investment horizons, and user-provided rationales such as technical analysis, business performance, and corporate actions. The data is enriched with user activity metrics, conviction levels, and prediction lifecycle statuses. By analyzing the collective sentiment and prediction accuracy of retail investors, this dataset offers valuable insights into crowd-driven market expectations and can be used to forecast short-term price movements, identify emerging trends, and enhance quantitative trading strategies through alternative data signals.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Deep Learning Chart-Based Alpha
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset leverages deep learning to predict future stock returns by mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders who analyze price charts. It transforms time series financial data into images (such as OHLC or other chart types) and applies pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to these images to generate return forecasts. The output includes both raw return predictions and quantile-based relative return rankings, along with associated probabilities. By capturing complex visual patterns and technical signals that may be overlooked by traditional quantitative models, this approach can identify non-linear relationships and subtle chart features that are predictive of price movements. The dataset is particularly useful for developing and testing alpha models that seek to exploit behavioral and technical trading signals, offering a novel perspective that complements standard factor-based or fundamental models.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Price Chart Continuation Pattern Similarity
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides daily, per-stock similarity scores that measure how closely a stock’s price chart matches well-known continuation-style technical patterns, such as flags, pennants, rectangles, channels, scallops, staircases, cup-and-handle, and gap formations. The scores are derived by comparing chart-image embeddings to a curated library of canonical continuation patterns using advanced machine learning techniques. Multiple summary statistics (mean, median, max, dynamic, etc.) are available across different time horizons and regions, enabling flexible analysis. These similarity scores can be used to identify stocks likely to resume their current trend after consolidation, support trend-following strategies, and enhance alpha generation by confirming or filtering trading signals. The dataset is particularly valuable for quantitative researchers seeking to incorporate pattern-based insights into predictive models for price movement forecasting.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Timely Corporate News Index
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a structured index of real-time corporate news releases from publicly listed companies, including details such as security codes, stock abbreviations, disclosure dates and times, titles, and document availability. By tracking the timing and frequency of official company announcements, investors and analysts can gauge market sentiment, anticipate volatility, and identify potential catalysts for price movements. The dataset is particularly useful for event-driven trading strategies, as timely disclosures often precede significant changes in stock prices due to new information entering the market.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Deep Learning Risk Free Returns
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict risk-free returns by transforming time series price and volume data into 2D chart images, which are then analyzed using pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The dataset includes predictions for multiple time horizons (such as 5, 10, 20, and 50 days) and provides both raw and relative return forecasts, along with quantile rankings and associated probabilities. By simulating a retail trader’s perspective through chart-based analysis, this dataset offers a unique, high-dimensional approach to forecasting future returns with minimal risk. It is particularly useful for identifying low-risk trading opportunities and enhancing portfolio construction by providing robust, model-driven signals that can help anticipate price movements in a risk-averse manner.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Earnings Date Data

Accurate mapping is essential for ensuring data consistency, reducing operational errors, and improving the reliability of multi-source analytics, which can indirectly enhance the precision of price movement predictions by ensuring correct security identification across datasets.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: International Findings Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset offers daily snapshots of international corporate events, including earnings announcements, conference calls, dividend declarations, shareholder meetings, and other key financial events. By tracking the timing and revisions of earnings dates, dividend actions, and other corporate events, the dataset enables researchers and traders to anticipate market-moving disclosures, identify signals of management intent, and exploit calendar-based trading strategies. Its forward-looking coverage and granular event data are valuable for predicting price movements, volatility spikes, and abnormal returns around scheduled corporate actions.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: International Equity Forum Activity

By analyzing trends in forum activity and sentiment, the dataset provides valuable insights into retail investor behavior and crowd sentiment, which can serve as leading indicators for price movements. The inclusion of risk-adjusted performance metrics and benchmark correlations further enhances its utility for developing predictive models and alpha strategies based on social media-driven market signals.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Text-Based Event Relationship Analysis
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset leverages advanced language models to extract and classify relationships between companies, events, and entities from unstructured text sources such as news articles, press releases, and corporate communications. By identifying the types and directions of these relationships, the dataset provides structured insights into how companies interact, form alliances, or respond to market developments. This information is valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in company relationships—such as mergers, partnerships, or competitive actions—often precede significant market reactions. The dataset enhances traditional event-driven strategies by offering a deeper, more nuanced understanding of the connections and influences within the market ecosystem.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Corporate Event Driven Stock Model
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a systematic stock-selection model that leverages corporate event data and machine learning techniques to predict future stock returns. It incorporates a wide range of event types, such as earnings announcements, executive changes, product launches, and structural corporate actions, and processes them using advanced feature engineering and algorithms like elastic net and xgBoost. The model outputs normalized scores and ranks for stocks based on the predictive impact of these events, enabling users to identify potential alpha opportunities and construct long/short portfolios. By capturing both fundamental and behavioral signals from event-driven market reactions, the dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, managing risk, and enhancing quantitative investment strategies.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Global Institutional Fund Holdings
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides daily, account-level insights into the holdings and transactions of major institutional investors, including mutual funds, ETFs, asset managers, pension funds, and insurance companies. It features detailed tables on daily trades, holdings, and the size of the investment account panel, with metrics such as conviction holdings, boundary trades, significant transactions, and concentration measures. By tracking changes in institutional ownership, trade activity, and portfolio concentration, the dataset enables users to identify shifts in market sentiment, detect accumulation or liquidation trends, and assess the impact of large fund movements on individual securities. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, understanding liquidity dynamics, and generating alpha through analysis of institutional behavior.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Japanese Corporate Governance Data

By evaluating factors like board effectiveness, ownership structure, and shareholder engagement, the dataset offers valuable insights into the governance quality of Japanese firms. Investors and analysts can use these governance metrics to identify companies with strong or weak governance practices, which can be predictive of future stock price movements, risk profiles, and long-term value creation.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive set of network-based momentum signals for global equities, combining traditional price momentum with advanced network analytics derived from business segments, geographic regions, analyst coverage, executive connections, innovation linkages, supply chain, and shipping data. The model leverages natural language processing on regulatory filings to identify economic linkages between companies, enhancing the predictive power and diversification of momentum strategies. By integrating multiple uncorrelated momentum factors and optimizing risk allocation, the dataset offers robust signals with higher risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdowns than conventional momentum approaches. Investors and analysts can use these insights to construct diversified portfolios and improve forecasts of future price movements.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Institutional Network Analysis Dataset
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive set of network-based momentum signals, constructed from multiple economic and textual networks such as business segments, geographic exposure, analyst coverage, executive links, patent innovation, supply chain, and shipping networks. Enhanced with natural language processing of company filings and EDGAR log-based relationships, the composite model aggregates these diverse factors using a risk parity approach. The resulting signals are designed to be less correlated with traditional momentum, offering improved risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdowns. This dataset is valuable for quantitative investors seeking to predict price movements by capturing complex inter-company relationships and alternative sources of momentum beyond price trends.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Financial Opinion Mining
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset focuses on financial opinion mining from various text-based sources such as earnings calls, news, and social media. It aims to extract potential signals by performing deep analysis, considering financial characteristics and correlations among different data sources. The methodology involves advanced feature extraction, sentiment scoring using word embeddings, semi-supervised/transfer learning for adapting sentiment across data, and time-series value prediction through multi-source embedding. The dataset is designed to cover opinion mining tasks including sentiment analysis, company grouping, and value prediction, ultimately seeking to uncover valuable insights from the complete event timeline across diverse text data.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Wikipedia Viewing Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset tracks daily Wikipedia pageviews for companies across a global universe, capturing user interest and information-seeking behavior. By aggregating and transforming raw pageview data into structured fields, it enables researchers to analyze trends in public attention, which can serve as a proxy for retail investor sentiment or information demand. The use of natural days (including weekends and holidays) ensures comprehensive coverage and more robust time series analysis. Spikes or sustained increases in pageviews may precede or coincide with significant price movements, making this dataset valuable for predicting market activity, especially around news events or periods of heightened public interest.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Thomson Reuters News Analytics Equities
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive news analytics for equities, including over 80 fields across five key categories: relevance, sentiment, novelty, volume, and headline classification. Each news item is scored for every asset it materially mentions, with separate linguistic processing for each asset, such as companies or commodities. The dataset includes granular metadata like timestamps, source, headline tags, and asset identifiers (RIC, PermID), enabling detailed analysis of how news impacts specific securities. By quantifying sentiment, relevance, and novelty, and tracking news volume, this dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying market-moving events, and generating alpha signals through systematic news-based strategies.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Archive News Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: New streaming and archive data for Benzinga, MT Newswires and an aggregated feed of global press releases and exchange disclosure wires.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Combined Alpha Model
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This Alpha Model (CAM) combines all similar alpha models in an optimal, static, linear combination. The weights assigned to each model vary by region.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Earnings and conference call data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between two major financial security identifiers: RIC (Reuters Instrument Code) and Bloomberg ID. Covering a wide range of global securities, it enables users to cross-reference and integrate data from different financial data providers and platforms. By facilitating seamless linkage of market data, pricing, and reference information across systems, this mapping is essential for data normalization, portfolio management, and multi-source analytics. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is a foundational resource for building robust, integrated datasets that support advanced financial modeling, risk analysis, and trading strategies.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Chart Pattern Similarity Scores
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides daily similarity scores that quantify how closely a stock’s recent price chart matches a range of canonical bilateral technical patterns, such as triangles, wedges, V-formations, and gap structures. By leveraging advanced image-based embeddings of OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) data, the dataset compares current price action to a curated library of reference patterns, producing scores for each pattern and aggregation method (mean, max, quantile, etc.) across multiple time horizons and global regions. These similarity scores help researchers and traders identify when a stock is exhibiting chart formations that historically precede significant price moves, either as continuations or reversals. The dataset is particularly valuable for developing and validating quantitative trading signals (alphas), as it enables systematic pattern recognition, supports cross-sectional and multi-horizon analysis, and can be integrated into machine learning models to enhance predictive power for future price movements.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Predictive Analyst-Company Signal Set
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides predictive signals specifically designed for advanced analyst and company relationship modeling, leveraging deep learning on company relations and analyst estimate data. It enhances traditional analyst revision and valuation models by integrating both company-to-company (Revere) and analyst-to-company (IBES) information, resulting in higher quality and broader coverage signals, especially for global equities. The dataset includes modules that generate forward-looking signals based on changes in analyst sentiment, earnings revisions, and valuation metrics, all informed by the underlying network of business relationships. These predictive signals can be used to anticipate future price movements by capturing both direct analyst actions and the economic linkages between companies, offering a unique edge for quantitative price prediction and alpha generation.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Deep Learning Price Signal Dataset
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides stock-level trading signals generated by optimizing traditional price and volume indicators using deep learning techniques. By rescaling and refining these indicators based on the unique properties of each instrument, the dataset aims to deliver uncorrelated alpha signals that enhance returns and Sharpe ratios. The data includes processed price, volume, and derived metrics, with robust handling of outliers and missing values. This resource is valuable for quantitative analysts and traders seeking to improve predictive accuracy and risk-adjusted performance in equity markets.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Price Volume Data for Equity
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: The dataset contains financial data related to equities, including metrics such as prices (open, high, low, close), trading volumes, market capitalization, returns, dividends, splits, and other key indicators that provide insights into stock performance and market activity.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Interval and MOO&MOC statistics
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive intraday market data at interval levels, including order imbalance events, quote and trade ticks, and detailed auction data for Market-On-Open (MOO) and Market-On-Close (MOC) sessions. It covers multiple global exchanges and includes fields such as bid/ask prices and sizes, trade prices and volumes, auction prices and volumes, and various qualifiers for trade and quote conditions. The dataset also tracks session-level statistics, volatility, VWAP, and order book dynamics. By analyzing order imbalances, auction outcomes, and interval-based price and volume movements, users can identify periods of heightened buying or selling pressure, anticipate price swings around auction events, and detect liquidity shifts. This information is highly valuable for predicting short-term price movements, understanding market microstructure, and developing intraday trading strategies.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Microstructure Spread Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive spread pricing data for securities traded across the US, Canada, and Asia. It includes key fields such as the ticker symbol, the spread (difference between bid and ask prices), and spread values calculated over the last 30 minutes, both in absolute terms and in basis points. By analyzing the spread and its recent changes, traders and analysts can gauge market liquidity, trading costs, and potential price volatility. Narrowing or widening spreads can signal shifts in supply-demand dynamics, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and identifying periods of heightened market activity.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Bond Yield Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive reference and pricing information for global corporate bonds, including historical data since 2006. It covers a wide range of attributes such as unique identifiers (ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL), issuer details, bond characteristics (coupon, maturity, callable/putable status), industry classifications, and extensive pricing fields (open, high, low, last, bid, ask, mid, volume, yields). The inclusion of corporate actions, structured note features, and regulatory indicators (such as IRS 871(m) compliance) makes it a robust resource for fixed income analysis. By leveraging this dataset, analysts can track bond performance, assess credit risk, monitor liquidity, and identify market trends, all of which are critical for predicting price movements and making informed investment decisions in the corporate bond market.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Relationship Data for Equity
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC), enabling users to link securities across Bloomberg and Refinitiv platforms. The data is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, and maintained for integration and operational purposes rather than general research. While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for harmonizing datasets, ensuring accurate cross-platform security identification, and supporting multi-source data analysis in quantitative research and portfolio management workflows.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Futures Market Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive daily data on the Kospi 200 Index, including index levels, constituent details, and corporate actions. It covers index values, market capitalization, sector and industry classifications, and detailed information on each constituent such as ISIN, market cap, free-float, and weights. The dataset also tracks changes due to rebalancing and corporate events, offering both end-of-day and next-day files. This rich set of index and constituent-level data is valuable for analyzing market trends, sector rotations, and the impact of index changes, making it a useful resource for predicting price movements of both the index and its underlying stocks, as well as for developing systematic trading strategies and risk models.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Holidays and Trading Hours Calendar
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: The Data Explorers dataset provides comprehensive short interest and securities lending data, sourced from the lending desks of major sell-side institutions and large buy-side players globally. It covers metrics such as lendable inventory, utilization rates, borrow demand, loan values, borrow costs, and proprietary sentiment indicators (e.g., DNS, DIPS, DIMV, DSS) at the security, group, and market level. The dataset includes both end-of-day and intraday feeds, with detailed breakdowns by region, asset class, and contributor type. By tracking the supply and demand dynamics of securities lending, as well as short positioning and borrow costs, this dataset offers valuable insights into market sentiment, short squeeze risk, and crowding. These signals are widely used in quantitative strategies to predict price reversals, identify crowded shorts, manage risk, and enhance alpha generation, making it a critical resource for anticipating price movements driven by short interest and lending market activity.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Corporate Bond Pricing Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of equity signals derived from corporate bond pricing data, including z-spread curves, term spreads, and principal component analysis factors such as shift, tilt, and twist. By linking bond market indicators—such as credit risk, yield curve dynamics, and bond-equity return divergences—to related equities, the dataset offers 19 base factors and several variants to predict future stock returns. These factors capture changes in credit conditions, market sentiment, and cross-asset relationships, making the dataset valuable for quantitative models, risk assessment, and alpha generation. Investors and analysts can use these signals to enhance equity selection, construct long-short strategies, and anticipate price movements based on underlying credit market trends.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Daily Spot and Cross Rate Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized global company fundamental data, covering 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and interim/quarterly financial statements, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and textual information for over 1500 data items. The data is point-in-time, capturing values as they were known historically, and supports peer comparability across regions and industries. With detailed income statements, balance sheets, cash flows, and supplemental metrics, this dataset enables robust analysis of company financial health, valuation, profitability, and risk. It is highly valuable for quantitative research, backtesting, and building predictive models to forecast price movements based on changes in fundamentals, financial ratios, and corporate actions.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Derived Industry Classification
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs, two of the most widely used security identifiers in the financial industry. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of data from different sources, facilitating more accurate and efficient data analysis. This mapping is particularly useful for analysts and portfolio managers who work with multi-vendor data feeds, as it ensures consistency in security identification across platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is essential for data normalization, aggregation, and the construction of robust multi-source trading and risk models.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Global Daily Pricing Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global fundamental financial data for public companies, combining FactSet Fundamentals, Reuters Knowledge Direct, and related symbology. It includes annual and interim financial statements, standardized and as-reported line items, per-share metrics, ratios, restatements, and point-in-time data, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for emerging markets. The data is mapped to unique identifiers (FactSet FSYM_ID, RIC, CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL) and supports cross-market and cross-vendor mapping. It enables robust historical analysis, backtesting, and quantitative modeling by offering clean, point-in-time, and restated financials, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements based on company fundamentals, valuation ratios, and financial health indicators.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Alternate Industry Classification
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides an alternative industry classification for global equities, derived from historical stock returns using principal component analysis (PCA) and robust resampling methods. By extracting significant risk factors and grouping securities into clusters of varying sizes, it offers a data-driven approach to industry segmentation across multiple regions and sectors. The dataset includes detailed mappings for top securities and supports flexible cluster sizes, enabling users to analyze market structure, sector rotation, and cross-sectional risk. This classification can enhance factor modeling, portfolio construction, and alpha generation by capturing dynamic relationships between stocks, potentially improving predictions of price movements and risk exposures.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Equity Interval Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides standardized, point-in-time operating metrics for companies worldwide, with deep industry-specific coverage (e.g., retail, airlines, oil & gas, healthcare, REITs). Metrics include key performance indicators such as same store sales, occupancy rates, production volumes, and other operational statistics, enabling detailed peer and cross-industry comparisons. The data is updated weekly and includes both annual and quarterly frequencies, with comprehensive historical coverage. By capturing granular, comparable operational data, this dataset is valuable for quantitative research and can enhance price prediction models by linking company performance drivers to future returns, especially when combined with financial statement and market data.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Specific Return Dataset
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides daily specific returns for global equities, calculated using a proprietary risk model that extends the Barra framework with additional style and industry factors. The data includes returns orthogonal to risk model factors, representing the idiosyncratic or residual component of asset performance. Coverage spans multiple regions and universes, with fields such as Bloomberg ID and specific return percentage. By decomposing total returns into factor-driven and residual parts, this dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to isolate stock-specific movements, assess alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted forecasting of price changes.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Relation Dataset
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive analyst earnings estimates and consensus data for over 60,000 global companies, including both current and historical forecasts. It aggregates detailed broker-level estimates, company-issued guidance, and consensus statistics such as mean, median, standard deviation, and revision counts for key financial measures like EPS, revenue, and cash flow. The data is enriched with industry classification (TRBC), company identifiers, and flags for accounting basis, currency, and reporting standards. By tracking estimate revisions, guidance surprises (beat/meet/miss), and the dispersion of analyst opinions, this dataset offers valuable forward-looking signals for price movement prediction, earnings surprise modeling, and quantitative investment strategies. Its breadth and granularity make it a foundational resource for backtesting, event studies, and real-time trading models sensitive to analyst sentiment and earnings momentum.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Multi-Domain Quantitative Factor Library
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset is a comprehensive library of quantitative factors designed for stock selection and risk modeling across global equities. It integrates hundreds of signals derived from regulatory filings, institutional ownership, sector-specific metrics, technical indicators, sentiment analysis, patent data, and alternative sources. The factors span multiple domains, including banking, technology, real estate, health care, and energy, and leverage both numerical and textual data using advanced techniques such as natural language processing and network analysis. By providing diverse, uncorrelated signals and sector-specific insights, the dataset enables investors and researchers to enhance alpha generation, improve risk management, and develop robust predictive models for price movements in various market environments.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Securities Lending and Short Market Dynamics Dataset
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers for financial securities. By linking these two widely used security identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv platforms. This mapping is essential for data normalization, portfolio management, and research workflows that require accurate identification and aggregation of securities across different data sources. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is a foundational resource for ensuring data consistency and reliability in quantitative models and trading systems.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Securities Lending Insight Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID) for global securities. It enables seamless integration and reconciliation of security data across different financial platforms and data sources. By facilitating accurate cross-referencing, the dataset supports portfolio management, trade processing, and data aggregation tasks. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is essential for ensuring data integrity and consistency when combining datasets for quantitative research, risk analysis, and multi-source analytics.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Forecast Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset delivers full order book and top of book tick-level statistics for global markets, including bid and ask levels, sizes, order updates, trade prices, volumes, and interval-based metrics. It aggregates and computes advanced measures such as average distances from mid, size distributions, and volatility at various intervals. By analyzing these detailed order book dynamics and trade flows, users can detect liquidity imbalances, order flow trends, and microstructure effects, which are instrumental in forecasting short-term price movements and understanding market behavior at a granular level.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Multi-Factor Model
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global equity ownership data, tracking holdings by institutions, mutual funds, insiders, and stakeholders. It aggregates information from regulatory filings such as SEC Form 13F, UK share registers, and other international sources, offering detailed position-level data including shares held, percentage ownership, and changes over time. The dataset enables analysis of institutional trading patterns, herding behavior, and the impact of ownership changes on stock returns. By monitoring shifts in institutional ownership and identifying high-conviction positions, researchers can gain insights into market sentiment, potential price movements, and the effectiveness of copycat or contrarian investment strategies. This data is valuable for constructing factors related to institutional activity, assessing market trends, and predicting future price movements based on changes in ownership structure.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Daily Specific Return Profiling Dataset
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized fundamental financial data for companies worldwide, covering over 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and interim/quarterly financial statements, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and extensive historical content. The data is point-in-time, capturing values as they were known at each reporting date, and includes restatements and amendments. With over 1,500 data items, it enables in-depth analysis of company performance, valuation, profitability, liquidity, leverage, and growth. The breadth and depth of coverage, along with proven peer comparability, make it a critical resource for building and backtesting quantitative models, identifying fundamental drivers of price movement, and constructing factor-based investment strategies.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Other Multi-Factor Risk Models
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of analyst estimates, actuals, recommendations, and price targets for over 60,000 companies. It includes both detailed (analyst-by-analyst) and consensus (mean, median, standard deviation) forecasts for key financial measures such as earnings per share (EPS), revenue, cash flow, dividends, and long-term growth. The data is updated daily and includes historical records, company-issued guidance, and surprise calculations (actual vs. consensus). With granular detail on estimate revisions, analyst and broker identities, and industry classifications, this dataset is essential for tracking market expectations, identifying earnings momentum, and quantifying earnings surprises—factors that are highly predictive of short-term and medium-term price movements. The breadth and timeliness of the data make it a cornerstone for quantitative models, event studies, and backtesting strategies that rely on forward-looking market sentiment and analyst behavior.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Rapid Search Interest Signals
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset captures real-time search interest data for specific companies and regions, using a standardized algorithm to transform hourly search trends into a continuous, unbounded metric. By estimating daily search activity from high-frequency data and providing a confidence score for each estimate, it enables timely detection of shifts in public attention or sentiment. Such rapid changes in search volume can serve as early indicators of market-moving events, news, or shifts in investor sentiment, making the dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and generating alpha signals.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: AI Sentiment Score Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive analytics on news items related to equities, including over 80 fields across five key categories: relevance, sentiment, novelty, volume, and headline classification. Each news item is processed to generate asset-specific scores, such as sentiment (positive, neutral, negative), relevance to the asset, and measures of news novelty and volume over various time windows. The dataset also includes metadata like headline tags, company identifiers, and timestamps. By quantifying the tone, frequency, and uniqueness of news coverage for each company, this dataset enables researchers and quantitative investors to systematically incorporate real-time and historical news sentiment into trading strategies. It is particularly useful for predicting short-term price movements, identifying momentum or reversal signals, and enhancing alpha models with alternative data reflecting market perception and information flow.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Textual Sentiment Analysis Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides daily sentiment scores for financial news headlines, generated by an in-house transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) model. It covers a wide range of companies and regions, offering granular sentiment classifications (positive, negative, neutral) along with confidence levels and descriptive statistics. The data is updated daily and structured in a matrix format, enabling researchers and quantitative analysts to efficiently incorporate real-time news sentiment into their trading and investment models. By quantifying the tone of news flow, the dataset helps identify shifts in market sentiment, anticipate price movements, and construct diversified alpha signals at both the company and market level.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Website Popularity Ranking Dataset
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive ranking of internet domains based on passive DNS traffic, capturing the relative activity of websites across a global network. Unlike traditional site ranking models that focus on browser-based traffic, this dataset measures the number of unique client IPs interacting with each domain, offering a protocol-agnostic view of internet engagement. Aggregated metrics such as top percentile rankings, skewness, and kurtosis help identify domains with unusual or concentrated activity. By tracking changes in domain activity and popularity, analysts can detect emerging trends, shifts in user behavior, and potential catalysts that may influence the price movements of companies associated with these domains.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Website Popularity Rankings
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides a robust, research-oriented ranking of the most popular websites worldwide, designed to be resistant to manipulation and volatility. It aggregates and harmonizes data from multiple sources, including DNS traffic, browser extensions, and web crawls, to produce a stable and reproducible list of top domains. The dataset includes detailed metrics such as relative popularity, ranking intervals, domain counts, and statistical measures like skewness and kurtosis. By mapping domains to standardized identifiers, it enables aggregation and analysis at various levels. This dataset is valuable for predicting price movements by identifying trends in web traffic, shifts in user behavior, and the emergence of influential domains, which can signal changes in market sentiment, consumer interest, or sector performance.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Webpage Views  Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset tracks daily Wikipedia page views for a global universe of companies, including both parent entities and their subsidiaries. By aggregating user interest across multiple languages and linking subsidiary activity to parent companies, it provides a unique measure of public attention and sentiment. Spikes or changes in page views can signal increased market interest, news events, or shifts in company visibility, which may precede trading activity or price movements. The dataset is especially useful for generating alternative sentiment signals and for event-driven trading strategies, as it captures real-time shifts in public focus that are not reflected in traditional financial data.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Securities Lending Files Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of securities lending activity across equities and fixed income instruments in over 110 countries. It aggregates transaction-level data from lending agents, third-party lenders, and beneficial owners, as well as borrowing activity from prime brokers and asset managers. Key fields include loan volumes, loan rates (average, min, max, and dispersion), utilization rates, collateral types, and borrowing activity ratings. The dataset also tracks the supply of shares available for lending, loan recalls, and rate changes, offering both daily and intraday granularity. By analyzing metrics such as utilization ratios, loan rate spikes, and borrowing demand, investors can identify securities under short-selling pressure, detect scarcity premiums, and anticipate potential price movements due to short squeezes or changes in market sentiment. This makes the dataset highly valuable for predicting price dynamics, managing risk, and developing alpha-generating strategies.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Daily Price Limit Data
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset provides daily information on stock trading halts and price limits for equities listed on the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Hong Kong exchanges, including constituents of the CSI 300 index. It contains fields such as security identifiers, exchange codes, trade dates, and the maximum and minimum allowable prices for each stock on a given day. By tracking when stocks hit their limit up or limit down prices, as well as when trading is halted, the dataset helps identify periods of abnormal market activity, liquidity constraints, and potential price reversals. Such insights are valuable for predicting short-term price movements, managing trading risk, and developing quantitative strategies sensitive to market imbalances.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: SmartHoldings Model
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset is a global stock selection model that ranks stocks based on the predicted future change in institutional ownership. It looks into various funds and creates their purchasing profile based on the underlying fundamental or technical factors of the companies it buys. Aggregation over different funds help predict future probable changes in institutional ownership of the stocks.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: socialmedia discussion
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset compiles user-generated comments, popularity rankings, and stock-specific discussion metrics for publicly traded Japanese securities. By aggregating daily data on likes, dislikes, comment counts, and unique user participation, it provides a comprehensive view of investor sentiment and engagement around individual stocks. The dataset is valuable for identifying shifts in market mood, tracking trending securities, and generating sentiment-based alpha signals. Analysts can leverage this information to anticipate price movements driven by retail investor activity and social sentiment, making it a useful tool for short-term trading strategies and market monitoring.

JPN_TOP1200_d1.name: Investor views
JPN_TOP1200_d1.description: This dataset tracks the co-search behavior of users on a major financial platform, capturing which companies are most frequently searched together by retail investors. By analyzing the top co-searched tickers for each focal stock, the data reveals patterns of investor attention, perceived relationships between companies, and potential information diffusion across stocks. Such insights can be valuable for predicting price movements, as spikes in co-search activity may signal increased investor interest, sector rotation, or anticipation of news events, all of which can lead to short-term price pressure or comovement among related stocks.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Corporate Acquisition Likelihood Model

By combining text-based signals with fundamental indicators, the model offers percentile scores across global, regional, sector, and industry levels, as well as flags for recent corporate actions. Investors and analysts can use these insights to identify potential takeover targets, anticipate price movements driven by acquisition speculation, and inform event-driven trading strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: AI Equity Alpha Forecasts
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides machine learning-driven forecasts of total return alpha for a broad universe of listed equities, with prediction horizons ranging from 1 to 12 months. The dataset delivers both daily and weekly updates, offering granular insights into the drivers of predicted returns. By combining forward-looking alpha scores with detailed factor breakdowns, this resource enables researchers and quantitative analysts to identify potential outperformers, understand the underlying reasons for forecasts, and enhance equity selection and risk management strategies. Its breadth and depth make it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing robust investment models.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: AI Enhanced Equity Factor Transfer
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset leverages advanced AI techniques to extract and transfer high-level equity factor features from a sophisticated quantitative research framework to other datasets. It includes a rich set of features such as price momentum, money flow strength, volume anomalies, liquidity alignment, and technical indicators like Bollinger Bands and Williams %R. Each feature is semantically defined and generated through AI-driven processes, ensuring clarity and consistency. By capturing nuanced interactions between price, volume, and liquidity, the dataset provides actionable signals for predicting price movements and constructing robust quantitative models. Its transfer learning approach enables the application of proven factor knowledge across diverse datasets, enhancing the predictive power and adaptability of investment strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: AI News Sentiment Scores
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily sentiment scores for global equities by analyzing news articles, press releases, and regulatory disclosures using a proprietary transformer-based natural language processing model. Covering thousands of companies across major regions, it quantifies the tone and relevance of news events, offering granular sentiment metrics at both the entity and event level. By systematically capturing shifts in market sentiment and event novelty, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify potential price-moving signals, enhance alpha generation, and improve risk management. Its comprehensive coverage and advanced scoring methodology make it a valuable resource for predicting short-term and medium-term asset returns based on news-driven market dynamics.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Performance-Weighted Analyst Estimates
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset applies an enhanced version of the StarMine SmartEstimate model to a broad universe of stocks and financial metrics, leveraging analyst estimate data from IBES. It calculates a performance score for each analyst based on their historical forecasting accuracy and incorporates the recency of their estimates. By combining these two factors, the model generates "smart estimates" that are more predictive than simple consensus means. The dataset includes modules for analyst innovation, outlier handling, and time-series feature generation, making it a robust tool for identifying which analyst forecasts are likely to be most accurate. This can help investors and researchers anticipate earnings surprises and price movements, as changes in smart estimates often precede market reactions.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: ESG scores
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBIDs), facilitating cross-platform security identification and data integration. By linking these two widely used financial identifiers, the dataset enables seamless aggregation and comparison of market data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv sources. This mapping is essential for portfolio managers, researchers, and trading systems that require accurate and efficient reconciliation of securities across different data vendors. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is crucial for ensuring data integrity and consistency in multi-source financial analysis, which underpins robust quantitative research and trading strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Estimations of Key Fundamentals
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily, regionally split files containing detailed and consensus analyst estimates for key financial metrics such as revenue, EBITDA, EPS, dividends, and price targets for publicly traded companies worldwide. It includes individual analyst and broker forecasts, consensus calculations (mean, median, high, low, standard deviation), and actuals, along with metadata on fiscal periods, reporting currencies, and company identifiers. The dataset is highly granular, supporting point-in-time analysis and backtesting, and is essential for identifying earnings surprises, revisions, and trends in analyst sentiment. By tracking changes in consensus and individual estimates, users can anticipate price movements driven by earnings releases, analyst upgrades/downgrades, and shifts in market expectations.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Earnings forecasts
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides bottom-up aggregated earnings forecasts and related financial metrics at the country, sector, industry, and index levels, covering 56 countries and major international indices with history back to 1985. It includes consensus analyst estimates for key measures such as EPS, revenue, book value, cash flow, dividends, P/E ratios, and long-term growth, all calendarized and available in local and common currencies. The data is structured to support global asset allocation, cross-border valuation, sector and industry analysis, and derivatives research. By tracking changes in consensus, estimate revisions, and aggregated sentiment, the dataset enables investors to identify under- or overvalued markets, monitor macro and sector trends, and anticipate shifts in market sentiment—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements at both the index and sector level.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Japan Analyst Estimate Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive earnings estimates for all listed and OTC Japanese companies, including both consolidated and non-consolidated figures. It covers fiscal year and interim (six-month) periods, offering forecasts and actuals for key financial metrics such as sales, operating profit, net profit, earnings per share, and dividends per share. The data is structured to allow point-in-time analysis and includes detailed flags for estimate sources, consolidation status, and dividend types. By tracking changes in analyst and company forecasts, as well as comparing estimates to actual results, this dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying earnings surprises, and constructing quantitative models for Japanese equities.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Analyst estimates & financial ratios
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset contains detailed point-in-time company financials, standardized ratios, earnings estimates, consensus recommendations, and business intelligence for global equities. It includes annual and interim financial statements, key ratios (such as ROE, ROA, debt-to-equity, margins), analyst estimates, and consensus ratings, as well as company reference data and officer information. The breadth and depth of financial metrics, combined with historical and restated data, allow for robust factor modeling, backtesting, and cross-sectional analysis. Researchers can use this dataset to identify value, growth, quality, and momentum signals, assess earnings surprises, and construct predictive models for price movements based on fundamental drivers and analyst sentiment.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Analyst Estimate Data for Equity
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides intraday updates of consensus financial estimates, actuals, and company guidance for over 16,000 global companies, sourced from more than 800 contributing brokers. It includes multiple daily delta files per region, allowing users to track real-time changes in analyst expectations for key financial metrics such as EPS, sales, dividends, cash flow, and industry-specific items. The dataset also offers daily historical consensus timelines, enabling analysis of estimate revisions, surprises, and trends. By capturing the latest market sentiment and analyst forecasts, this data is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying earnings momentum, and responding to market-moving events as they unfold.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Analyst Trade Ideas
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating cross-platform identification of securities. It is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring high coverage and accuracy. While not intended for general research or direct price prediction, this mapping is essential for data integration, enabling analysts and portfolio managers to link and synchronize datasets from different vendors. By ensuring consistent instrument identification, it supports robust multi-source analytics, backtesting, and the construction of unified trading universes, which are foundational for any quantitative or fundamental price movement analysis.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Fundamental Analyst Estimates
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global companies, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for developing markets. The dataset includes restatements, detailed line items, and standardized fields, enabling robust cross-company and cross-market comparisons. Key fields include balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as derived ratios such as return on equity, margins, and growth rates. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and predictive modeling, as it allows users to track historical financial performance, identify trends, and build factor models that can help forecast future price movements based on company fundamentals.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Corporate Earning Estimates Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset comprises earnings estimates for Japanese companies, produced by a large group of financial journalists. It includes both projected and actual financial results, covering a wide range of listed, OTC, and emerging market companies in Japan. The dataset is updated frequently, with estimates released just before official earnings announcements, and contains detailed financial metrics such as sales, operating profit, net income, EPS, dividends, and more. By providing a neutral, third-party perspective on corporate earnings, this dataset can help investors anticipate earnings surprises, gauge market sentiment, and improve the accuracy of price movement predictions around earnings season.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Analyst Estimate Daily Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID), facilitating cross-platform security identification. It is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring broad coverage and accuracy. The mapping enables users to link securities across different data providers and trading systems, which is essential for portfolio management, trade reconciliation, and data integration tasks. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is crucial for ensuring data consistency and enabling the use of multiple datasets in quantitative research and trading strategies.
