ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Analyst Estimates Base Reference
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset serves as a placeholder or reference point for the foundational data underlying analyst estimates and key performance indicators, without containing any actual financial or market data itself. Its primary function is to facilitate access to industry classifications and essential metadata required for quantitative research, while avoiding penalization for using common base modules in research workflows. Although it does not provide direct content, it enables seamless integration of industry and company classification information, which is crucial for constructing and interpreting analyst-driven signals and for ensuring consistency in backtesting and model development. By supporting the structural backbone for more detailed analyst and KPI datasets, it indirectly aids in the accurate prediction of price movements through proper sector and industry alignment.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Standardized Analyst Consensus Forecasts
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides standardized, cleaned, and event-aligned analyst consensus forecasts and actuals for global equities, enabling direct comparison across companies and time. It aggregates and harmonizes consensus data from multiple leading sources, including I/B/E/S, Capital IQ, and FactSet, and applies rigorous data cleaning to remove expired or irrelevant forecasts. The dataset supports flexible configuration for different forecast horizons (quarterly, annual, rolling) and includes both forecast and actual values, as well as surprise calculations. By offering time-series event data with consistent methodology, it allows users to track revisions, analyze forecast accuracy, and construct robust quantitative models. This makes it a valuable resource for predicting price movements, backtesting strategies, and understanding market expectations versus realized outcomes.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Global Analyst Earnings Forecasts
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global analyst earnings forecasts, consensus estimates, and actuals for over 60,000 companies, sourced from broker and sell-side analyst submissions. It includes detailed and summary-level data on key financial metrics such as earnings per share (EPS), revenue, cash flow, and segment-level results, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The dataset tracks both current and historical estimates, revisions, and company-issued guidance, with extensive metadata on contributors, accounting standards, and industry classifications. By aggregating and updating analyst expectations in near real-time, this dataset enables users to monitor market sentiment, identify earnings momentum, and anticipate potential surprises—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing quantitative investment strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Global Analyst Factor Signals
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of analyst-derived quantitative factors and indicators for global equities, constructed using standardized methodologies. It leverages consensus estimates, actuals, and revision data from multiple sources to generate a wide range of predictive signals, such as estimate momentum, earnings surprise, and analyst recommendation trends. The dataset is designed to be comparable across regions and time, with rigorous data cleaning and normalization. By offering both raw and composite factors—similar to those used in established quantitative models—this resource enables users to systematically test and implement alpha strategies, enhance risk models, and improve the forecasting of price movements based on analyst behavior and expectations.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Multi Horizon Analyst Revision Signals
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides decomposed analyst revision signals across short, medium, and long time horizons, derived from a comprehensive analyst revision-based stock ranking model. By applying advanced signal processing techniques, it extracts horizon-specific components from a wide array of analyst-driven metrics, such as earnings estimate changes, recommendation shifts, and predicted surprises. The resulting fields enable researchers and investors to isolate and analyze the impact of analyst sentiment and estimate revisions over different time frames, enhancing the ability to identify timely alpha opportunities and anticipate price movements driven by changes in analyst outlook. This multi-horizon approach is particularly valuable for constructing and testing trading strategies that are sensitive to the timing and persistence of analyst-driven signals.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Behavioral Finance Signal Factors
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a suite of behavioral finance-based signals designed to capture investor extrapolation bias in equity markets. It includes six key factors: three that analyze the shape and curvature of price paths, and three that identify salient patterns such as streaks in returns, extreme daily movements, and visually prominent trends. By quantifying how investors may irrationally project recent performance into the future, these signals serve as contrarian indicators and can help forecast short-term reversals and momentum effects. The dataset is valuable for predictive modeling, risk assessment, and portfolio construction, offering insights into market inefficiencies driven by psychological biases and aiding in the identification of potential mispricings and alpha opportunities.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: user predictions from Minkabu
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset aggregates stock price predictions made by retail investors across major social media platforms in Japan, Europe, and China. It includes detailed records of buy/sell recommendations, target prices, investment horizons, and user-provided rationales such as technical analysis, business performance, and corporate actions. The data is enriched with user activity metrics, conviction levels, and prediction lifecycle statuses. By analyzing the collective sentiment and prediction accuracy of retail investors, this dataset offers valuable insights into crowd-driven market expectations and can be used to forecast short-term price movements, identify emerging trends, and enhance quantitative trading strategies through alternative data signals.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Deep Learning Chart-Based Alpha
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset leverages deep learning to predict future stock returns by mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders who analyze price charts. It transforms time series financial data into images (such as OHLC or other chart types) and applies pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to these images to generate return forecasts. The output includes both raw return predictions and quantile-based relative return rankings, along with associated probabilities. By capturing complex visual patterns and technical signals that may be overlooked by traditional quantitative models, this approach can identify non-linear relationships and subtle chart features that are predictive of price movements. The dataset is particularly useful for developing and testing alpha models that seek to exploit behavioral and technical trading signals, offering a novel perspective that complements standard factor-based or fundamental models.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Price Chart Continuation Pattern Similarity
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily, per-stock similarity scores that measure how closely a stock’s price chart matches well-known continuation-style technical patterns, such as flags, pennants, rectangles, channels, scallops, staircases, cup-and-handle, and gap formations. The scores are derived by comparing chart-image embeddings to a curated library of canonical continuation patterns using advanced machine learning techniques. Multiple summary statistics (mean, median, max, dynamic, etc.) are available across different time horizons and regions, enabling flexible analysis. These similarity scores can be used to identify stocks likely to resume their current trend after consolidation, support trend-following strategies, and enhance alpha generation by confirming or filtering trading signals. The dataset is particularly valuable for quantitative researchers seeking to incorporate pattern-based insights into predictive models for price movement forecasting.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Timely Corporate News Index
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a structured index of real-time corporate news releases from publicly listed companies, including details such as security codes, stock abbreviations, disclosure dates and times, titles, and document availability. By tracking the timing and frequency of official company announcements, investors and analysts can gauge market sentiment, anticipate volatility, and identify potential catalysts for price movements. The dataset is particularly useful for event-driven trading strategies, as timely disclosures often precede significant changes in stock prices due to new information entering the market.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Deep Learning Risk Free Returns
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict risk-free returns by transforming time series price and volume data into 2D chart images, which are then analyzed using pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The dataset includes predictions for multiple time horizons (such as 5, 10, 20, and 50 days) and provides both raw and relative return forecasts, along with quantile rankings and associated probabilities. By simulating a retail trader’s perspective through chart-based analysis, this dataset offers a unique, high-dimensional approach to forecasting future returns with minimal risk. It is particularly useful for identifying low-risk trading opportunities and enhancing portfolio construction by providing robust, model-driven signals that can help anticipate price movements in a risk-averse manner.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Earnings Date Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs and Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating the cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. By enabling seamless integration of data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv, it supports analysts and portfolio managers in consolidating and validating security identifiers for research, trading, and risk management. Accurate mapping is essential for ensuring data consistency, reducing operational errors, and improving the reliability of multi-source analytics, which can indirectly enhance the precision of price movement predictions by ensuring correct security identification across datasets.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: International Findings Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset offers daily snapshots of international corporate events, including earnings announcements, conference calls, dividend declarations, shareholder meetings, and other key financial events. It provides detailed metadata such as event status, timing, fiscal period, and confirmation level, along with links to press releases and filings. By tracking the timing and revisions of earnings dates, dividend actions, and other corporate events, the dataset enables researchers and traders to anticipate market-moving disclosures, identify signals of management intent, and exploit calendar-based trading strategies. Its forward-looking coverage and granular event data are valuable for predicting price movements, volatility spikes, and abnormal returns around scheduled corporate actions.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: International Equity Forum Activity
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset compiles user engagement and sentiment metrics from a wide range of online forums dedicated to equity discussions across multiple countries and languages. It includes aggregated statistics such as active user counts, comment volumes, buy and sell ratings, and unique user participation for various financial instruments. By analyzing trends in forum activity and sentiment, the dataset provides valuable insights into retail investor behavior and crowd sentiment, which can serve as leading indicators for price movements. The inclusion of risk-adjusted performance metrics and benchmark correlations further enhances its utility for developing predictive models and alpha strategies based on social media-driven market signals.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Text-Based Event Relationship Analysis
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset leverages advanced language models to extract and classify relationships between companies, events, and entities from unstructured text sources such as news articles, press releases, and corporate communications. By identifying the types and directions of these relationships, the dataset provides structured insights into how companies interact, form alliances, or respond to market developments. This information is valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in company relationships—such as mergers, partnerships, or competitive actions—often precede significant market reactions. The dataset enhances traditional event-driven strategies by offering a deeper, more nuanced understanding of the connections and influences within the market ecosystem.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Corporate Event Driven Stock Model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a systematic stock-selection model that leverages corporate event data and machine learning techniques to predict future stock returns. It incorporates a wide range of event types, such as earnings announcements, executive changes, product launches, and structural corporate actions, and processes them using advanced feature engineering and algorithms like elastic net and xgBoost. The model outputs normalized scores and ranks for stocks based on the predictive impact of these events, enabling users to identify potential alpha opportunities and construct long/short portfolios. By capturing both fundamental and behavioral signals from event-driven market reactions, the dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, managing risk, and enhancing quantitative investment strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Global Institutional Fund Holdings
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily, account-level insights into the holdings and transactions of major institutional investors, including mutual funds, ETFs, asset managers, pension funds, and insurance companies. It features detailed tables on daily trades, holdings, and the size of the investment account panel, with metrics such as conviction holdings, boundary trades, significant transactions, and concentration measures. By tracking changes in institutional ownership, trade activity, and portfolio concentration, the dataset enables users to identify shifts in market sentiment, detect accumulation or liquidation trends, and assess the impact of large fund movements on individual securities. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, understanding liquidity dynamics, and generating alpha through analysis of institutional behavior.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Management and Executive Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive biographical and professional information on board members and senior executives from companies worldwide. It includes details such as employment history, education, achievements, compensation, board roles, committee memberships, and network connections across organizations. By analyzing board composition, director expertise, compensation structures, and interlocking directorates, investors and researchers can assess governance quality, leadership stability, and potential strategic shifts. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in executive leadership, board structure, or director networks often precede significant corporate actions, impact investor sentiment, and influence firm performance.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Japanese Corporate Governance Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive corporate governance ratings and detailed governance-related data for Japanese listed companies. It includes both aggregate and issue-level scores, covering aspects such as board structure, director independence, diversity, compensation transparency, shareholder rights, and the presence of governance-related scandals. The data is derived from company disclosures and public events, using both qualitative and quantitative methods. By evaluating factors like board effectiveness, ownership structure, and shareholder engagement, the dataset offers valuable insights into the governance quality of Japanese firms. Investors and analysts can use these governance metrics to identify companies with strong or weak governance practices, which can be predictive of future stock price movements, risk profiles, and long-term value creation.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Direct Fundamental Data

Key fields cover balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as detailed breakdowns of assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, and key performance indicators. FactSet’s symbology enables robust cross-referencing with other datasets. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and model development, as it allows researchers to track company financial health, valuation, and performance over time, supporting predictive modeling of price movements based on changes in core financial metrics.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Global Seasonal Regime Return Signals
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides predictive return signals for global equities by modeling the impact of calendar seasonality, corporate event timing, market regime context, and key data sources such as price-volume, analyst forecasts, options, and fundamentals. Each module isolates a specific data aspect—like price-volume trends, analyst revisions, or option-implied signals—and overlays contextual features such as month/quarter effects, proximity to earnings or guidance events, and prevailing market regimes (e.g., risk-on/off, expansion/contraction). The dataset is strictly point-in-time and D1-lagged to avoid lookahead bias, making it robust for research and production use. By enabling detailed analysis of how individual features and market contexts drive return predictions, it supports advanced quantitative modeling, event studies, and adaptive strategies across diverse market conditions.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Global Insider Transaction Features

It covers multiple regions and asset classes, with detailed metadata such as transaction type, insider role, ownership connection, trade significance, and post-transaction holdings. By aggregating and analyzing these transactions, the dataset enables the identification of potentially informative trades, such as opportunistic buying or selling, which can signal future price movements due to information asymmetry. Quantitative models and event studies built on this data can help forecast abnormal returns, enhance alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted portfolio performance by leveraging the predictive power of insider activity.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Institutions and Beneficial Stake Ownership
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global equity ownership by institutions, mutual funds, and beneficial stakeholders. It includes current and historical holdings data from over 50,000 portfolios and companies across 70 countries, with more than 10 years of history. Key fields cover shares held, percent of shares outstanding, report dates, aggregated statistics, and investor profiles. The dataset enables analysis of institutional buying and selling activity, ownership concentration, and changes in major holders, which are critical for understanding market sentiment, liquidity, and potential price movements. By tracking shifts in institutional positions and identifying new or reduced stakes, investors and researchers can anticipate trends, detect accumulation or distribution phases, and enhance predictive models for stock price behavior.

By processing interval-level trading statistics—such as bid-ask spreads, order book depth, trade counts, volatility, and volume—into daily summaries, it enables consistent cross-regional analysis despite differences in exchange hours and data structures. These features are valuable for quantitative researchers and portfolio managers seeking to generate alpha signals, as they capture nuanced intraday market dynamics that can precede price movements. The dataset’s unified format and broad coverage make it a powerful tool for predicting short-term price changes and enhancing trading strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Index Reconstitution Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global index reconstitution events, including the addition and deletion of stocks or companies from various equity indexes, their respective weight percentages, and detailed hedge ratio data. It covers dynamic and static hedge ratios for both indexes and currencies, as well as currency pair exposures and effective dates. The dataset also includes metrics such as momentum and interest rates, along with position weights and returns for index components. By tracking changes in index composition, weights, and hedging strategies, this dataset enables analysts to identify shifts in market sentiment, sector rotation, and currency risk management, which are critical for forecasting price movements and understanding the impact of index rebalancing on asset prices.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Machine Learning Factor Projections
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides machine learning-generated projection features for US equities, leveraging advanced neural network architectures such as multi-layer perceptrons, self-attention mechanisms, and convolutional neural networks. It synthesizes a wide array of quantitative factor models—including value, growth, momentum, quality, liquidity, and management quality—by integrating both traditional financial metrics and alternative data sources. The resulting features are designed to capture complex, non-linear relationships in the data, offering enhanced predictive signals for future price movements. By combining insights from multiple factor themes and updating models with new data, this dataset can help investors identify stocks with favorable risk-return profiles and anticipate shifts in market trends, making it a valuable tool for systematic portfolio construction and alpha generation.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Multilingual NLP News Sentiment Signals
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides enriched sentiment signals for financial news by leveraging a scalable, multilingual natural language processing (NLP) framework. Initially built on top of Benzinga news and designed to expand to other text-based sources, it distills insights from large language models into efficient, production-ready NLP pipelines. The dataset includes fields such as average character count, AFINN and Loughran-McDonald sentiment scores, and supports coverage for the top 3000 US stocks. By offering standardized, high-frequency sentiment metrics across multiple languages and news sources, this dataset enables quantitative researchers and traders to systematically capture shifts in market sentiment, identify news-driven trading opportunities, and enhance predictive models for price movements.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Analysts rating model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, algorithmically generated ratings and evaluations for over 6,000 equities and 15,000 funds worldwide. It aggregates and processes fundamental, technical, and projected criteria to produce objective scores on upside potential and risk, including metrics such as earnings revision trends, price potential, medium-term technical trends, and relative performance. Additionally, it offers risk assessments based on historical bear market and bad news sensitivity. The multi-factor approach enables investors and researchers to identify stocks with strong growth prospects, favorable technical momentum, and manageable risk, making it a valuable resource for predicting price movements and constructing robust investment strategies.

By aggregating diverse quantitative signals and leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, this dataset enables systematic investors to identify stocks with high expected returns, manage risk, and time factor exposures, making it a powerful tool for predicting price movements and constructing outperforming equity portfolios.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Stock Selection from Accounting-based Factors
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset contains a comprehensive suite of Performance Deviation Index (PDI) factors derived from 14 key accounting variables, designed to measure the deviation of a company's latest financial metrics from its historical averages. The dataset includes composite models, quality-focused variants, and sector-neutralized signals, all constructed using advanced techniques such as risk parity weighting, deseasonalization, and clustering. By capturing anomalies and behavioral biases in financial statement data, these factors have demonstrated superior risk-adjusted returns compared to traditional accounting ratios and growth metrics. The dataset is valuable for quantitative investors seeking to enhance stock selection, improve portfolio diversification, and boost predictive power for price movements across global equity markets.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Sensitivity to the Inflation Change
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides stock-level sensitivity estimates to expected inflation, using changes in breakeven rates and advanced machine learning techniques such as elastic net regression. It covers a wide range of global equities and includes sector, country, and performance metrics, allowing users to analyze how individual stocks and sectors respond to inflationary pressures. By quantifying inflation beta and related exposures, the dataset is valuable for portfolio managers and analysts seeking to forecast price movements, manage risk, and implement tactical asset allocation strategies in environments with changing inflation expectations.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Interest Rate Sensitivity Measures
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a stock-level measure of interest rate sensitivity using a forward-looking discounted cash flow (DCF) approach. By simulating changes in discount rates and incorporating analyst forecasts, it quantifies how sensitive a company's valuation is to shifts in interest rates. The dataset includes key metrics such as implied cost of equity, elasticity to rate changes, and sector-neutralized scores, making it highly relevant for understanding how macroeconomic shifts—especially in interest rates—may impact equity prices. Investors and analysts can use this information to identify stocks that are more or less vulnerable to rising rates, construct hedged portfolios, and enhance alpha generation by anticipating market reactions to monetary policy changes.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Stock Selection DL model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides the outputs of a next-generation deep learning model designed for global stock selection with a focus on statistical arbitrage and mean reversion alpha. It includes both raw and processed model scores, updated daily and with monthly historical data, covering a broad universe of equities across multiple regions. The model leverages advanced neural network architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, transformers, and conformers, and is engineered to be interpretable and relatively uncorrelated with common equity style factors. The dataset is particularly valuable for systematic and high-frequency trading strategies, as it offers timely, actionable signals that can be used to enhance portfolio construction, manage risk, and exploit short-term price inefficiencies. By providing robust, data-driven alpha signals, this dataset can help predict price movements and improve trading performance.

By monitoring the buying and selling activities of company officers, directors, and major shareholders, the dataset provides valuable signals of insider sentiment and potential future price movements. Analysts can use this data to identify patterns of accumulation or distribution by key stakeholders, which often precede significant market moves, making it a powerful tool for predicting stock performance and investor behavior in Asian equities.

By identifying stocks likely to experience increased or decreased institutional buying, the dataset offers valuable signals for long/short strategies, portfolio construction, and risk management. Its predictive power is supported by backtesting, showing positive returns and high Sharpe Ratios, making it a robust tool for forecasting price movements driven by institutional flows.

By combining these perspectives, the dataset provides percentile rankings (1-100) for stocks globally, enabling investors to identify companies with both robust, sustainable earnings and positive analyst sentiment. Each event is tagged by topic (such as M&A, earnings guidance, product launches, regulatory actions, and more) and assigned a significance level, allowing users to filter for the most impactful news. The data includes detailed headlines, descriptions, event categorization, and metadata such as timing, company identifiers, and industry classification. By offering structured, noise-filtered news with intelligent tagging, this dataset enables quantitative models and event-driven strategies to quickly identify and react to market-moving information, making it a valuable resource for predicting short-term price movements and volatility.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: MnA Deals Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset offers detailed information on mergers and acquisitions (M&A), new equity issues, and debt offerings, including deal structure, participants, financial terms, and status. It covers transaction attributes such as deal value, premiums, payment methods, industry classifications, and advisor involvement. By tracking deal flow, market trends, and competitive dynamics, the dataset enables users to analyze market share, identify comparable transactions, and assess the impact of corporate actions on stock prices. It is highly valuable for predicting price movements around deal announcements, understanding industry consolidation, and constructing event-driven trading strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Significant Developments Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news and market-moving events, systematically tagged by topic and significance. Covering a wide range of event types—such as mergers, acquisitions, product launches, regulatory actions, earnings guidance, and management changes—it enables users to filter out noise and focus on impactful developments. Each event is categorized by importance and topic, allowing for integration into quantitative models and historical trend analysis. By tracking and analyzing these significant corporate events, researchers and investors can better anticipate price movements, identify event-driven trading opportunities, and enhance alpha generation strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: News Analytics on Equities
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive analytics on news items related to equities, including sentiment, relevance, novelty, and volume scores for each asset mentioned in a news article. It covers over 80 fields, such as headline classification, asset identifiers, sentiment probabilities, and volume counts, enabling granular analysis of how news impacts individual companies and commodities. By quantifying the tone and relevance of news, as well as tracking the frequency and uniqueness of coverage, the dataset allows researchers and portfolio managers to assess the potential influence of news flow on price movements, identify momentum or reversal signals, and enhance predictive models for asset returns.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: News Analytics Data

The mapping is essential for integrating and reconciling data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv sources, enabling seamless data aggregation, analysis, and reporting. While not directly predictive of price movements, this dataset is crucial for ensuring data consistency and accuracy in multi-source quantitative research, portfolio management, and trading systems that rely on identifiers from both platforms.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: News Analytic Model Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset delivers real-time and historical financial news, blogs, and sentiment analytics sourced from thousands of global websites and media outlets. It includes structured metadata such as headlines, story content, assigned and derived tickers/topics, market-moving potential indicators, sentiment scores, readership metrics, and corporate event details. Advanced natural language processing and machine learning models generate analytics like market-moving news probability, sentiment, and novelty scores for each story. By quantifying news impact and sentiment, this dataset enables users to identify market-moving events, gauge investor sentiment, and detect abnormal price movement risks, making it highly valuable for predicting short-term price reactions and supporting event-driven trading strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Relevant News Analytics Data

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Real Time News Feed Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time financial statement data for a global universe of public companies, including both active and inactive firms. It offers daily historical snapshots of income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, capturing both originally reported and restated values as they were known on each reporting date. The data is standardized for cross-company comparability and includes detailed metadata such as auditor opinions, industry classifications, and currency conversions. By eliminating forward-looking and survivorship biases, this dataset enables accurate backtesting and robust factor research, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements based on fundamental signals and historical financial trends.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Story by Story Sentiment
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides sentiment analysis at the individual news story level, offering granular sentiment scores such as positivity, negativity, fear, financial up/down, hype, volatility, certainty, and uncertainty for each news article. The data is available intraday, daily, and hourly, and covers thousands of securities across major global regions. By tracking sentiment shifts in real time and at high frequency, this dataset enables users to detect market-moving news, gauge investor mood, and anticipate price movements based on the tone and content of news coverage. The detailed entity-level sentiment and volume metrics further enhance predictive modeling for short-term and event-driven trading strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Textual News Feed Data

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Headline Sentiment Analysis using DNN
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset leverages advanced machine learning techniques to transfer sentiment signals from one news analytics dataset to another, specifically mapping sentiment derived from one set of financial news headlines onto a different set of press release headlines. By using neural network models to learn how sentiment is constructed in the source dataset and applying this understanding to the target dataset, it generates a new, alternative sentiment score for each press release. This approach enables the creation of a unique sentiment signal that may capture market-relevant nuances missed by traditional sentiment models. Such a dataset can be valuable for predicting price movements, as it provides a differentiated view of market sentiment that can be used to enhance alpha generation, inform trading strategies, and improve risk assessment by identifying shifts in investor mood not visible through standard sentiment analytics.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: News Sentiment Analysis using DNN
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset applies neural network techniques to transfer sentiment analytics from one news dataset to another, specifically mapping sentiment from tr_trna_eq headlines to ravenpack_web_v2 headlines. By leveraging machine learning to align sentiment scoring methodologies across datasets, it generates new sentiment signals for the target dataset, potentially enhancing alpha generation and predictive power. This approach allows for the creation of unified sentiment indicators, improving the consistency and robustness of trading models that rely on news-driven sentiment for forecasting price movements.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Deep Learning News Sentiment Signals
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides enhanced sentiment signals derived from financial news and social media text using advanced deep learning techniques. By leveraging a large corpus of news articles and social media posts, the dataset applies multiple language embeddings and a deep neural network trained on millions of samples to classify sentiment related to companies and market events. The output includes sentiment scores and other text-based features, offering a refined view of market mood and reactions. These signals can be used to anticipate price movements by capturing shifts in investor sentiment and market perception, making the dataset valuable for quantitative trading strategies and risk assessment.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: News Sentiment Signal Features
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides granular sentiment and NLP-derived features extracted from individual news stories and financial articles. It includes metrics such as polarity, readability, subjectivity, and various sentiment scores (positive, negative, fear, certainty, uncertainty, financial up/down, hype, volatility) at both story and entity levels. The data is available at intraday, daily, and hourly intervals, covering thousands of securities across major regions. By quantifying the emotional and informational tone of news in real time, these features can help analysts and models anticipate market reactions, identify sentiment-driven price movements, and enhance alpha generation strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Transferred News Sentiment Analytics
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides sentiment analytics for financial news by transferring sentiment scores from a comprehensive news sentiment source to a major financial news feed using advanced machine learning techniques. It covers global equities and commodities, offering asset-level sentiment classifications (positive, neutral, negative) for news items, along with relevance, novelty, and volume metrics. By leveraging both the breadth of the original sentiment dataset and the timeliness of the target news feed, it enables more robust and timely sentiment signals for stocks and other assets. These signals can be used to anticipate price movements, identify market-moving news, and enhance quantitative trading strategies by integrating real-time sentiment shifts with historical context.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Global Equity Premarket Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset captures global equity premarket information, including company details, market status, and exchange listings. It excludes securities with inactive or delisted statuses, focusing on actively traded instruments before the official market open. The data includes fields such as ticker, currency, lot size, and exchange codes, providing a snapshot of premarket activity and corporate actions. By offering early insights into market sentiment, liquidity, and potential trading opportunities, this dataset can help analysts anticipate price movements and identify actionable trends prior to regular trading hours.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Sensitivity to Interest Rates Model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a machine learning-based model that quantifies the sensitivity of individual stocks to changes in interest rates, using elastic net regression. It includes metrics such as sensitivity to parallel shifts (level) and twists (slope) of the yield curve, derived from principal component analysis of global interest rate data. Covering over 11,000 stocks across 45 countries, the dataset enables investors to assess how monetary policy changes and yield curve movements may impact stock returns. By incorporating these sensitivity measures into portfolio construction and risk management, users can better predict price movements during periods of interest rate volatility and optimize exposure to macroeconomic factors.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Multi-Region Dividend Alpha Model Dataset
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset contains the outputs and components of a machine learning-based global stock selection model focused on dividend-paying equities. Leveraging a large factor library and advanced algorithms, it generates composite scores that reflect the expected performance and risk profile of stocks, with specialized sub-models for linear, hedge, and defensive scenarios. The model incorporates contextual information, risk management, and signal persistence metrics, making it highly effective for constructing portfolios that seek stable income and downside protection. By providing predictive signals and risk-adjusted rankings, this dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, optimizing portfolio returns, and managing risk in dividend-oriented investment strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Outstanding Short Positions for Japanese Equities
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily outstanding short selling positions for stocks listed on the Japan Exchange Group, which includes the Tokyo and Osaka Stock Exchanges. It contains detailed information such as the ratio of short positions to shares outstanding, the number of shares sold short, the names and addresses of short sellers and investment contractors, and historical reporting data. By tracking changes in short interest across a broad universe of Japanese equities, the dataset helps analysts identify stocks with rising or falling bearish sentiment, potential short squeezes, and market trends. This information is valuable for predicting price movements, assessing market risk, and developing trading strategies based on short interest dynamics.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Dividend prediction model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC), serving as a cross-reference for security identifiers across two major financial data vendors. The data is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring comprehensive coverage and accuracy. While primarily intended for operational and data management purposes rather than direct research or trading signal generation, this mapping is essential for integrating datasets, reconciling positions, and ensuring consistency in multi-vendor environments. Accurate identifier mapping can indirectly support price prediction by enabling seamless merging of disparate datasets, thus improving the quality and breadth of input data for quantitative models and research workflows.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Japanese PnL Guidance
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive historical record of forward-looking financial guidance issued by companies listed on Japanese stock exchanges. It includes detailed data on revenue, operating profit (EBIT), recurring profit, profit before tax, net profit, and earnings per share (EPS), as well as dividend forecasts at various fiscal intervals. The dataset captures both the quantitative targets and the qualitative reasons for changes in guidance, offering insights into management expectations and strategic adjustments. By tracking the timing and magnitude of guidance revisions, analysts can assess market sentiment, anticipate earnings surprises, and identify potential catalysts for price movements, making this dataset a valuable tool for forecasting stock performance and constructing predictive trading signals.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Dividend model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset identifies and predicts companies most likely to reduce, suspend, or terminate their dividend payments, focusing on so-called "dividend laggards." Leveraging a global factor library and machine learning algorithms, the model analyzes historical and real-time data to flag firms at risk of dividend cuts, which often precede significant share price declines and continued underperformance. By providing early warning signals on potential dividend reductions, the dataset is valuable for investors seeking to avoid downside risk, implement short strategies, or optimize portfolio yield, especially during periods of economic stress when dividend suspensions become more prevalent.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Intraday FX rates
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized company financial statement data and key performance metrics for a global universe of public companies, with daily point-in-time snapshots and deep historical coverage. It includes annual and interim/quarterly income statements, balance sheets, cash flow statements, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and textual information, all mapped to a consistent schema for cross-company and cross-country comparability. The dataset supports robust backtesting and factor research by eliminating survivorship and look-ahead bias, and is especially valuable for quantitative models and systematic strategies seeking to predict price movements based on changes in company fundamentals, valuation ratios, profitability, leverage, and other financial health indicators.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Linked Firms Momentum Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive set of network-based momentum signals for global equities, combining traditional price momentum with advanced network analytics derived from business segments, geographic regions, analyst coverage, executive connections, innovation linkages, supply chain, and shipping data. The model leverages natural language processing on regulatory filings to identify economic linkages between companies, enhancing the predictive power and diversification of momentum strategies. By integrating multiple uncorrelated momentum factors and optimizing risk allocation, the dataset offers robust signals with higher risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdowns than conventional momentum approaches. Investors and analysts can use these insights to construct diversified portfolios and improve forecasts of future price movements.

Enhanced with natural language processing of company filings and EDGAR log-based relationships, the composite model aggregates these diverse factors using a risk parity approach. The resulting signals are designed to be less correlated with traditional momentum, offering improved risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdowns. This dataset is valuable for quantitative investors seeking to predict price movements by capturing complex inter-company relationships and alternative sources of momentum beyond price trends.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Financial Opinion Mining
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset focuses on financial opinion mining from various text-based sources such as earnings calls, news, and social media. It aims to extract potential signals by performing deep analysis, considering financial characteristics and correlations among different data sources. The methodology involves advanced feature extraction, sentiment scoring using word embeddings, semi-supervised/transfer learning for adapting sentiment across data, and time-series value prediction through multi-source embedding. The dataset is designed to cover opinion mining tasks including sentiment analysis, company grouping, and value prediction, ultimately seeking to uncover valuable insights from the complete event timeline across diverse text data.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Wikipedia Viewing Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset tracks daily Wikipedia pageviews for companies across a global universe, capturing user interest and information-seeking behavior. By aggregating and transforming raw pageview data into structured fields, it enables researchers to analyze trends in public attention, which can serve as a proxy for retail investor sentiment or information demand. The use of natural days (including weekends and holidays) ensures comprehensive coverage and more robust time series analysis. Spikes or sustained increases in pageviews may precede or coincide with significant price movements, making this dataset valuable for predicting market activity, especially around news events or periods of heightened public interest.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Thomson Reuters News Analytics Equities
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive news analytics for equities, including over 80 fields across five key categories: relevance, sentiment, novelty, volume, and headline classification. Each news item is scored for every asset it materially mentions, with separate linguistic processing for each asset, such as companies or commodities. The dataset includes granular metadata like timestamps, source, headline tags, and asset identifiers (RIC, PermID), enabling detailed analysis of how news impacts specific securities. By quantifying sentiment, relevance, and novelty, and tracking news volume, this dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying market-moving events, and generating alpha signals through systematic news-based strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Earnings and conference call data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between two major financial security identifiers: RIC (Reuters Instrument Code) and Bloomberg ID. Covering a wide range of global securities, it enables users to cross-reference and integrate data from different financial data providers and platforms. By facilitating seamless linkage of market data, pricing, and reference information across systems, this mapping is essential for data normalization, portfolio management, and multi-source analytics. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is a foundational resource for building robust, integrated datasets that support advanced financial modeling, risk analysis, and trading strategies.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Chart Pattern Similarity Scores
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily similarity scores that quantify how closely a stock’s recent price chart matches a range of canonical bilateral technical patterns, such as triangles, wedges, V-formations, and gap structures. By leveraging advanced image-based embeddings of OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) data, the dataset compares current price action to a curated library of reference patterns, producing scores for each pattern and aggregation method (mean, max, quantile, etc.) across multiple time horizons and global regions. These similarity scores help researchers and traders identify when a stock is exhibiting chart formations that historically precede significant price moves, either as continuations or reversals. The dataset is particularly valuable for developing and validating quantitative trading signals (alphas), as it enables systematic pattern recognition, supports cross-sectional and multi-horizon analysis, and can be integrated into machine learning models to enhance predictive power for future price movements.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Predictive Analyst-Company Signal Set
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides predictive signals specifically designed for advanced analyst and company relationship modeling, leveraging deep learning on company relations and analyst estimate data. It enhances traditional analyst revision and valuation models by integrating both company-to-company (Revere) and analyst-to-company (IBES) information, resulting in higher quality and broader coverage signals, especially for global equities. The dataset includes modules that generate forward-looking signals based on changes in analyst sentiment, earnings revisions, and valuation metrics, all informed by the underlying network of business relationships. These predictive signals can be used to anticipate future price movements by capturing both direct analyst actions and the economic linkages between companies, offering a unique edge for quantitative price prediction and alpha generation.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Deep Learning Price Signal Dataset
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides stock-level trading signals generated by optimizing traditional price and volume indicators using deep learning techniques. By rescaling and refining these indicators based on the unique properties of each instrument, the dataset aims to deliver uncorrelated alpha signals that enhance returns and Sharpe ratios. The data includes processed price, volume, and derived metrics, with robust handling of outliers and missing values. This resource is valuable for quantitative analysts and traders seeking to improve predictive accuracy and risk-adjusted performance in equity markets.

The dataset also tracks session-level statistics, volatility, VWAP, and order book dynamics. By analyzing order imbalances, auction outcomes, and interval-based price and volume movements, users can identify periods of heightened buying or selling pressure, anticipate price swings around auction events, and detect liquidity shifts. This information is highly valuable for predicting short-term price movements, understanding market microstructure, and developing intraday trading strategies.

It includes key fields such as the ticker symbol, the spread (difference between bid and ask prices), and spread values calculated over the last 30 minutes, both in absolute terms and in basis points. By analyzing the spread and its recent changes, traders and analysts can gauge market liquidity, trading costs, and potential price volatility. Narrowing or widening spreads can signal shifts in supply-demand dynamics, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and identifying periods of heightened market activity.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Bond Yield Data

It covers a wide range of attributes such as unique identifiers (ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL), issuer details, bond characteristics (coupon, maturity, callable/putable status), industry classifications, and extensive pricing fields (open, high, low, last, bid, ask, mid, volume, yields). The inclusion of corporate actions, structured note features, and regulatory indicators (such as IRS 871(m) compliance) makes it a robust resource for fixed income analysis. By leveraging this dataset, analysts can track bond performance, assess credit risk, monitor liquidity, and identify market trends, all of which are critical for predicting price movements and making informed investment decisions in the corporate bond market.

While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for harmonizing datasets, ensuring accurate cross-platform security identification, and supporting multi-source data analysis in quantitative research and portfolio management workflows.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Holidays and Trading Hours Calendar
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: The Data Explorers dataset provides comprehensive short interest and securities lending data, sourced from the lending desks of major sell-side institutions and large buy-side players globally. It covers metrics such as lendable inventory, utilization rates, borrow demand, loan values, borrow costs, and proprietary sentiment indicators (e.g., DNS, DIPS, DIMV, DSS) at the security, group, and market level. The dataset includes both end-of-day and intraday feeds, with detailed breakdowns by region, asset class, and contributor type. By tracking the supply and demand dynamics of securities lending, as well as short positioning and borrow costs, this dataset offers valuable insights into market sentiment, short squeeze risk, and crowding. These signals are widely used in quantitative strategies to predict price reversals, identify crowded shorts, manage risk, and enhance alpha generation, making it a critical resource for anticipating price movements driven by short interest and lending market activity.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Corporate Bond Pricing Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of equity signals derived from corporate bond pricing data, including z-spread curves, term spreads, and principal component analysis factors such as shift, tilt, and twist. By linking bond market indicators—such as credit risk, yield curve dynamics, and bond-equity return divergences—to related equities, the dataset offers 19 base factors and several variants to predict future stock returns. These factors capture changes in credit conditions, market sentiment, and cross-asset relationships, making the dataset valuable for quantitative models, risk assessment, and alpha generation. Investors and analysts can use these signals to enhance equity selection, construct long-short strategies, and anticipate price movements based on underlying credit market trends.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Derived Industry Classification
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs, two of the most widely used security identifiers in the financial industry. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of data from different sources, facilitating more accurate and efficient data analysis. This mapping is particularly useful for analysts and portfolio managers who work with multi-vendor data feeds, as it ensures consistency in security identification across platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is essential for data normalization, aggregation, and the construction of robust multi-source trading and risk models.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Global Daily Pricing Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global fundamental financial data for public companies, combining FactSet Fundamentals, Reuters Knowledge Direct, and related symbology. It includes annual and interim financial statements, standardized and as-reported line items, per-share metrics, ratios, restatements, and point-in-time data, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for emerging markets. The data is mapped to unique identifiers (FactSet FSYM_ID, RIC, CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL) and supports cross-market and cross-vendor mapping. It enables robust historical analysis, backtesting, and quantitative modeling by offering clean, point-in-time, and restated financials, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements based on company fundamentals, valuation ratios, and financial health indicators.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Alternate Industry Classification
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides an alternative industry classification for global equities, derived from historical stock returns using principal component analysis (PCA) and robust resampling methods. By extracting significant risk factors and grouping securities into clusters of varying sizes, it offers a data-driven approach to industry segmentation across multiple regions and sectors. The dataset includes detailed mappings for top securities and supports flexible cluster sizes, enabling users to analyze market structure, sector rotation, and cross-sectional risk. This classification can enhance factor modeling, portfolio construction, and alpha generation by capturing dynamic relationships between stocks, potentially improving predictions of price movements and risk exposures.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Equity Interval Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides standardized, point-in-time operating metrics for companies worldwide, with deep industry-specific coverage (e.g., retail, airlines, oil & gas, healthcare, REITs). Metrics include key performance indicators such as same store sales, occupancy rates, production volumes, and other operational statistics, enabling detailed peer and cross-industry comparisons. The data is updated weekly and includes both annual and quarterly frequencies, with comprehensive historical coverage. By capturing granular, comparable operational data, this dataset is valuable for quantitative research and can enhance price prediction models by linking company performance drivers to future returns, especially when combined with financial statement and market data.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Specific Return Dataset
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily specific returns for global equities, calculated using a proprietary risk model that extends the Barra framework with additional style and industry factors. The data includes returns orthogonal to risk model factors, representing the idiosyncratic or residual component of asset performance. Coverage spans multiple regions and universes, with fields such as Bloomberg ID and specific return percentage. By decomposing total returns into factor-driven and residual parts, this dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to isolate stock-specific movements, assess alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted forecasting of price changes.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Relation Dataset
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive analyst earnings estimates and consensus data for over 60,000 global companies, including both current and historical forecasts. It aggregates detailed broker-level estimates, company-issued guidance, and consensus statistics such as mean, median, standard deviation, and revision counts for key financial measures like EPS, revenue, and cash flow. The data is enriched with industry classification (TRBC), company identifiers, and flags for accounting basis, currency, and reporting standards. By tracking estimate revisions, guidance surprises (beat/meet/miss), and the dispersion of analyst opinions, this dataset offers valuable forward-looking signals for price movement prediction, earnings surprise modeling, and quantitative investment strategies. Its breadth and granularity make it a foundational resource for backtesting, event studies, and real-time trading models sensitive to analyst sentiment and earnings momentum.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Corporate Action Dataset
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset looks at corporate events that can affect stock prices, such as delisting, merger, stock splits, etc. One can analyze the effect of corporate actions on stock prices and develop alphas based on event-driven opportunities.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Multi-Domain Quantitative Factor Library
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset is a comprehensive library of quantitative factors designed for stock selection and risk modeling across global equities. It integrates hundreds of signals derived from regulatory filings, institutional ownership, sector-specific metrics, technical indicators, sentiment analysis, patent data, and alternative sources. The factors span multiple domains, including banking, technology, real estate, health care, and energy, and leverage both numerical and textual data using advanced techniques such as natural language processing and network analysis. By providing diverse, uncorrelated signals and sector-specific insights, the dataset enables investors and researchers to enhance alpha generation, improve risk management, and develop robust predictive models for price movements in various market environments.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Securities Lending Insight Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID) for global securities. It enables seamless integration and reconciliation of security data across different financial platforms and data sources. By facilitating accurate cross-referencing, the dataset supports portfolio management, trade processing, and data aggregation tasks. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is essential for ensuring data integrity and consistency when combining datasets for quantitative research, risk analysis, and multi-source analytics.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Forecast Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset delivers full order book and top of book tick-level statistics for global markets, including bid and ask levels, sizes, order updates, trade prices, volumes, and interval-based metrics. It aggregates and computes advanced measures such as average distances from mid, size distributions, and volatility at various intervals. By analyzing these detailed order book dynamics and trade flows, users can detect liquidity imbalances, order flow trends, and microstructure effects, which are instrumental in forecasting short-term price movements and understanding market behavior at a granular level.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Multi-Factor Model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global equity ownership data, tracking holdings by institutions, mutual funds, insiders, and stakeholders. It aggregates information from regulatory filings such as SEC Form 13F, UK share registers, and other international sources, offering detailed position-level data including shares held, percentage ownership, and changes over time. The dataset enables analysis of institutional trading patterns, herding behavior, and the impact of ownership changes on stock returns. By monitoring shifts in institutional ownership and identifying high-conviction positions, researchers can gain insights into market sentiment, potential price movements, and the effectiveness of copycat or contrarian investment strategies. This data is valuable for constructing factors related to institutional activity, assessing market trends, and predicting future price movements based on changes in ownership structure.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Specific return of extended factors
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of analyst earnings estimates, company-issued guidance, and actual reported financials for over 60,000 companies. It includes both detailed and consensus forecasts for key financial metrics such as EPS, revenue, cash flow, and dividends, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The data is updated daily and includes historical records, point-in-time snapshots, and restated values to avoid look-ahead and survivorship bias. Industry classification is available via TRBC, and the dataset supports granular analysis by region, sector, and fiscal period. By tracking estimate revisions, consensus trends, and the relationship between guidance and market expectations, this dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements around earnings announcements, identifying sentiment shifts, and constructing alpha models based on analyst behavior and forecast dispersion.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Rapid Search Interest Signals
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset captures real-time search interest data for specific companies and regions, using a standardized algorithm to transform hourly search trends into a continuous, unbounded metric. By estimating daily search activity from high-frequency data and providing a confidence score for each estimate, it enables timely detection of shifts in public attention or sentiment. Such rapid changes in search volume can serve as early indicators of market-moving events, news, or shifts in investor sentiment, making the dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and generating alpha signals.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: AI Sentiment Score Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive analytics on news items related to equities, including over 80 fields across five key categories: relevance, sentiment, novelty, volume, and headline classification. Each news item is processed to generate asset-specific scores, such as sentiment (positive, neutral, negative), relevance to the asset, and measures of news novelty and volume over various time windows. The dataset also includes metadata like headline tags, company identifiers, and timestamps. By quantifying the tone, frequency, and uniqueness of news coverage for each company, this dataset enables researchers and quantitative investors to systematically incorporate real-time and historical news sentiment into trading strategies. It is particularly useful for predicting short-term price movements, identifying momentum or reversal signals, and enhancing alpha models with alternative data reflecting market perception and information flow.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Textual Sentiment Analysis Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily sentiment scores for financial news headlines, generated by an in-house transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) model. It covers a wide range of companies and regions, offering granular sentiment classifications (positive, negative, neutral) along with confidence levels and descriptive statistics. The data is updated daily and structured in a matrix format, enabling researchers and quantitative analysts to efficiently incorporate real-time news sentiment into their trading and investment models. By quantifying the tone of news flow, the dataset helps identify shifts in market sentiment, anticipate price movements, and construct diversified alpha signals at both the company and market level.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Website Popularity Ranking Dataset
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive ranking of internet domains based on passive DNS traffic, capturing the relative activity of websites across a global network. Unlike traditional site ranking models that focus on browser-based traffic, this dataset measures the number of unique client IPs interacting with each domain, offering a protocol-agnostic view of internet engagement. Aggregated metrics such as top percentile rankings, skewness, and kurtosis help identify domains with unusual or concentrated activity. By tracking changes in domain activity and popularity, analysts can detect emerging trends, shifts in user behavior, and potential catalysts that may influence the price movements of companies associated with these domains.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Website Popularity Rankings
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides a robust, research-oriented ranking of the most popular websites worldwide, designed to be resistant to manipulation and volatility. It aggregates and harmonizes data from multiple sources, including DNS traffic, browser extensions, and web crawls, to produce a stable and reproducible list of top domains. The dataset includes detailed metrics such as relative popularity, ranking intervals, domain counts, and statistical measures like skewness and kurtosis. By mapping domains to standardized identifiers, it enables aggregation and analysis at various levels. This dataset is valuable for predicting price movements by identifying trends in web traffic, shifts in user behavior, and the emergence of influential domains, which can signal changes in market sentiment, consumer interest, or sector performance.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Webpage Views  Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset tracks daily Wikipedia page views for a global universe of companies, including both parent entities and their subsidiaries. By aggregating user interest across multiple languages and linking subsidiary activity to parent companies, it provides a unique measure of public attention and sentiment. Spikes or changes in page views can signal increased market interest, news events, or shifts in company visibility, which may precede trading activity or price movements. The dataset is especially useful for generating alternative sentiment signals and for event-driven trading strategies, as it captures real-time shifts in public focus that are not reflected in traditional financial data.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Daily Price Limit Data
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset provides daily information on stock trading halts and price limits for equities listed on the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Hong Kong exchanges, including constituents of the CSI 300 index. It contains fields such as security identifiers, exchange codes, trade dates, and the maximum and minimum allowable prices for each stock on a given day. By tracking when stocks hit their limit up or limit down prices, as well as when trading is halted, the dataset helps identify periods of abnormal market activity, liquidity constraints, and potential price reversals. Such insights are valuable for predicting short-term price movements, managing trading risk, and developing quantitative strategies sensitive to market imbalances.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: SmartHoldings Model
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset is a global stock selection model that ranks stocks based on the predicted future change in institutional ownership. It looks into various funds and creates their purchasing profile based on the underlying fundamental or technical factors of the companies it buys. Aggregation over different funds help predict future probable changes in institutional ownership of the stocks.

ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.name: Sentiment Data for Equity
ASI_MINVOL1M_d1.description: This dataset aggregates and analyzes social media posts and news articles related to financial markets, covering thousands of sources and several years of historical data. It quantifies market sentiment and buzz for individual assets, sectors, and indices using advanced natural language processing and machine learning techniques. The data includes sentiment scores, buzz indicators, and trading signals, which are statistically validated and can be used to identify shifts in market mood, anticipate volatility, and generate actionable buy/sell signals. By monitoring real-time and historical sentiment, traders and analysts can enhance their price movement predictions and improve portfolio performance through timely, data-driven decisions.
