IND_TOP500_d1.name: Interval and MOO&MOC statistics
IND_TOP500_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive intraday market data at interval levels, including order imbalance events, quote and trade ticks, and detailed auction data for Market-On-Open (MOO) and Market-On-Close (MOC) sessions. It covers multiple global exchanges and includes fields such as bid/ask prices and sizes, trade prices and volumes, auction prices and volumes, and various qualifiers for trade and quote conditions. The dataset also tracks session-level statistics, volatility, VWAP, and order book dynamics. By analyzing order imbalances, auction outcomes, and interval-based price and volume movements, users can identify periods of heightened buying or selling pressure, anticipate price swings around auction events, and detect liquidity shifts. This information is highly valuable for predicting short-term price movements, understanding market microstructure, and developing intraday trading strategies.

IND_TOP500_d1.name: Microstructure Spread Data
IND_TOP500_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive spread pricing data for securities traded across the US, Canada, and Asia. It includes key fields such as the ticker symbol, the spread (difference between bid and ask prices), and spread values calculated over the last 30 minutes, both in absolute terms and in basis points. By analyzing the spread and its recent changes, traders and analysts can gauge market liquidity, trading costs, and potential price volatility. Narrowing or widening spreads can signal shifts in supply-demand dynamics, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and identifying periods of heightened market activity.

IND_TOP500_d1.name: Bond Yield Data
IND_TOP500_d1.description: This dataset provides comprehensive reference and pricing information for global corporate bonds, including historical data since 2006. It covers a wide range of attributes such as unique identifiers (ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL), issuer details, bond characteristics (coupon, maturity, callable/putable status), industry classifications, and extensive pricing fields (open, high, low, last, bid, ask, mid, volume, yields). The inclusion of corporate actions, structured note features, and regulatory indicators (such as IRS 871(m) compliance) makes it a robust resource for fixed income analysis. By leveraging this dataset, analysts can track bond performance, assess credit risk, monitor liquidity, and identify market trends, all of which are critical for predicting price movements and making informed investment decisions in the corporate bond market.

IND_TOP500_d1.name: Futures Market Data

The dataset also tracks changes due to rebalancing and corporate events, offering both end-of-day and next-day files. This rich set of index and constituent-level data is valuable for analyzing market trends, sector rotations, and the impact of index changes, making it a useful resource for predicting price movements of both the index and its underlying stocks, as well as for developing systematic trading strategies and risk models.

IND_TOP500_d1.name: Holidays and Trading Hours Calendar
IND_TOP500_d1.description: The Data Explorers dataset provides comprehensive short interest and securities lending data, sourced from the lending desks of major sell-side institutions and large buy-side players globally. The dataset includes both end-of-day and intraday feeds, with detailed breakdowns by region, asset class, and contributor type. By tracking the supply and demand dynamics of securities lending, as well as short positioning and borrow costs, this dataset offers valuable insights into market sentiment, short squeeze risk, and crowding. These signals are widely used in quantitative strategies to predict price reversals, identify crowded shorts, manage risk, and enhance alpha generation, making it a critical resource for anticipating price movements driven by short interest and lending market activity.

This mapping is particularly useful for analysts and portfolio managers who work with multi-vendor data feeds, as it ensures consistency in security identification across platforms. IND_TOP500_d1.name: Alternate Industry Classification

The dataset includes detailed mappings for top securities and supports flexible cluster sizes, enabling users to analyze market structure, sector rotation, and cross-sectional risk. This classification can enhance factor modeling, portfolio construction, and alpha generation by capturing dynamic relationships between stocks, potentially improving predictions of price movements and risk exposures.

IND_TOP500_d1.name: Specific Return Dataset

Coverage spans multiple regions and universes, with fields such as Bloomberg ID and specific return percentage. By decomposing total returns into factor-driven and residual parts, this dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to isolate stock-specific movements, assess alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted forecasting of price changes.

Its breadth and granularity make it a foundational resource for backtesting, event studies, and real-time trading models sensitive to analyst sentiment and earnings momentum.
